title: Brief intervention for stressful life situations and complex minimal cerebral dysfunctions
summary: As part of the study, a three-session brief intervention will be conducted with participants who present with complex Minimal Cerebral Dysfunctions (MCD) or who are currently experiencing stressful life situations. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either a coaching intervention based on the Selection, Optimization, and Compensation (SOC) model to support the management of MCD-related challenges, or a coaching intervention focused on wisdom-oriented strategies for coping with perceived stressful life circumstances. Over the course of the three sessions, a concrete individual coaching goal will be collaboratively identified and pursued with each participant. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of the wisdom-based intervention in comparison to the SOC-based brief intervention.
conditions: Complex minimal cerebral dysfunctions or psychological distress due to stressful life circumstances

interventions.name: Arm 1: Intervention based on the model of Selection, Optimization, and Compensation (Baltes & Baltes), with a focus on complex minimal cerebral dysfunctions (3 sessions of 50 minutes each).
Arm 2: Intervention based on the psychological concept of wisdom, with a focus on wisdom-related coping with stressful life circumstances (3 sessions of 50 minutes each).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimal cerebral dysfunction or demanding life circumstances
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality, insufficient German language skills
